name: messenger-testimonial

frames.best_why: Four messages with reaction chips, the live status bar and all three metric tiles sit fully in frame.

tagline: Customer praise plays out as a live chat thread with emoji reactions.
summary: A pale page holding a narrow messenger window where a support conversation types itself out one message at a time. Bubbles carry avatars, names and times, reactions pop underneath, and live stats sit at the bottom.
appearance: Off-white page with a bold heading and grey intro above a slim chat column bordered by thin rules. Inside: a white pill with a green dot, alternating grey and black rounded bubbles with round avatars and faint times, tiny emoji chips, then a live-status bar and three metric tiles.
behaviour: Messages arrive in sequence, each preceded by three bouncing typing dots, and spring up with their avatar. Clicking a bubble toggles a small emoji reaction chip under it, while the pulse dot and the online count stay in motion.
demo_content: Heading "Live Customer Conversations" and messages from Emily Chen, Team Lab, Markus T. and Sarah K.
search_phrases: testimonials shown as a chat thread
messages that appear one by one
use_when: A support or SaaS page wants testimonials that feel like a live conversation rather than static quote cards.
avoid_when: The whole script, names and reactions are hardcoded, and autoplay on load cannot be turned off by the reader.
customise: All five messages, senders, avatars, times and reaction sets are in a hardcoded array; the timing, colours and pulse dots need source edits.
weight_why: Five messages and a couple of pulsing status dots; nothing heavy runs.

a11y.note: Reaction chips toggle from click handlers on plain divs, so keyboard users cannot open them; no reduced-motion handling.

issues: As more messages arrive the footer bar and metric tiles drop below the frame.
Timestamps are 9px light grey and the sender names are very faint.
polish_why: Convincing chat thread with reactions and live stats; tiny timestamps and the page growing too tall.
